title: Quote DD's effectiveness from the 2026-10 trials, with their caveats; never the September minutes
body: DD's measured effectiveness is in two trials: the 15-task Claude Sonnet 5.5 trial (docs/guide/how-it-works.md, "How it is measured": same resolution, +7 quality points, every project requirement met, +1% cost against the agent alone) and the Opus 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 trial at high effort (docs/benchmarks/2026-10-v2-trial-opus-haiku.md: every condition met every requirement, a ceiling, with DD the cheapest condition for both models). Quote them with their caveats: one project, small samples, the second a ceiling. Do not quote the September 2026 agent trial's minutes (72.4 against 37.3): one 25-minute timeout in one task produced that gap, and the 84% token saving of the replay scenarios measures context cost, not task success. Why: a reader of a summary block reports a 2x speedup one outlier produced; the write-ups carry the caveats beside the numbers, the summaries do not.
not_derivable: The numbers sit in the docs; which claims the data cannot support is written only here and in the trial write-ups' caveats.
